verdicts.claim: structureRamp.ts:780 — `const next = Math.min(clamped, cursor.frame + steps);` — the cursor 'only ever walks UP one frame at a time' (root_cause wording).

verdicts.claim: ⛔ HEADLINE — the proposed value 1 BREAKS R182-D ('you don't skip them'), a documented owner ruling in SPARK_CANON.md:301. The sim drains 0–3 ticks per RENDERED frame; the renderer syncs once per rendered frame; at ticksPerFrame 3 the cursor can never advance more than one plate per draw, at 1 it can advance three.
verdicts.note: NOT IN THE REPORT AT ALL. main.ts:2673-2674 `const dtSec = Math.min(tickerObj.deltaMS / 1000, 0.05); physicsAccumulator += dtSec;` then :2697 `while (physicsAccumulator >= PHYSICS_DT)`; PHYSICS_DT = 1/60 (physicsLoop.ts:81). So a rendered frame drains up to 3 sim ticks (the 0.05 clamp). `structureRampRenderer.sync(world)` is called ONCE per ticker frame at main.ts:4014, outside that loop. Therefore the drawn sequence advances by `floor(ticks_elapsed_since_last_draw / ticksPerFrame)` plates per DRAW. At per=3 the worst case (3 ticks) is exactly 1 plate — no plate can ever be skipped on screen, on any machine. At per=1 a 30 Hz display or any 33 ms frame drains 2 ticks and the player sees 12 of the 24 plates; a hitch-clamped frame skips 3. The value 3 is exactly matched to the 0.05 clamp; the report never discovered that property and its fix destroys it. ⛔ This is the S182 §2 hole in its purest form: structureRamp.test.ts:349-360 advances `tick` by exactly 1 per call, so it hardcodes a 1 tick : 1 observation ratio the real loop does not guarantee — the very test the report nominates as its 'regression hold' CANNOT see this. per=2 halves the exposure (only a 3-tick hitch skips); per=1 maximises it.

verdicts.claim: structureRamp.ts:776 — `if (clamped <= cursor.frame) return { frame: clamped, sinceTick: tick };` proves ticksPerFrame governs CATCH-UP only, so a gradual chew is 'UNAFFECTED' and the sequence is 'identical at ticksPerFrame 1 and 3'.
verdicts.note: Line :776 verbatim and the catch-up/target distinction is real. But 'unaffected' overreaches. When the target is ONE frame ahead (the ordinary chew), :778-779 still gate on `per`: at per=3 the cursor holds the old plate for up to 2 extra ticks before stepping; at per=1 it steps on the next tick. The set of frames VISITED is identical; the frame drawn AT A GIVEN TICK is not. The report's proposed new test ('the cursor's frame sequence is identical at ticksPerFrame 1 and 3') is therefore only true under a careful reading of 'sequence' and will be written wrong by a session that takes the sentence at face value.

verdicts.claim: …and therefore 'the natural lead-in is `per - 1` ticks, so NO new lead-in constant is needed' for the owner's 'millisecond of delay'.
verdicts.note: ⛔ THE REPORT'S OWN ARGUMENT KILLS ITS OWN RECOMMENDED VALUE. While healthy the cursor re-anchors `sinceTick` to now every frame (:776). On the lethal hit, `steps = floor((tick - sinceTick)/per) = floor(1/per)`. At per=3 that is 0 → the plate holds ~2 ticks before the run starts (the lead-in). At per=1 it is 1 → the run starts on the very next tick and the lead-in is ZERO. The owner_item explicitly asks for 'a tiny lead-in and THEN the frames run through a lot quicker'. per=1 delivers the second half and deletes the first. per=2 keeps 1 tick (17 ms) of it.

verdicts.claim: tests_owed — 'the regression hold `expect(seen).toEqual(...24 frames...)` at :358 proves quicker must not become skipped'.

What it under-budgets: (a) two RED assertions at its own recommended value (`structureRamp.test.ts:377-382`) that must be re-pinned, and re-pinning them at per=1 means rewriting a probe whose 30-tick observation now exceeds the entire 23-tick run; (b) an 18th file (`e2e/hub-ramp-art.spec.ts`); (c) the coverage-gate re-pin at `hubSelfDestructS182.test.ts:345`; (d) if the branch takes the render-loop hazard seriously — and it should — a new test that drives `advanceRampCursor` at 2 and 3 ticks per observation rather than 1, which is a genuinely new fixture, not a one-liner. Still Standard, but the 'only two lines of real code' framing will read to a branch as half a day and it is not.
net_assessment:
⭐ THE REPORT IS MOSTLY RIGHT AND ITS BEST WORK IS REAL — AND ITS RECOMMENDED NUMBER IS THE WRONG ONE. Every one of the 13 evidence entries exists at the cited file:line and says what is claimed; I opened all of them. The refutation of the brief's hypothesis is correct and valuable: R182-D was built in S182, the cursor is real (`structureRampRenderer.ts:208`), render-local (`:80`), pruned (`:327`), and nothing is skipped in the arithmetic. The rebuild-reverts-the-fix trap in `assets-source/*/atlas-specs.json` is a genuine catch I confirmed against both builders. The HUB_DEATH_RUN_TICKS no-op argument is sound: the poll re-anchors exactly (`hostTick.ts:707`), so 30 >= 24 and 30 >= 8 really are the same verdict. Root-causing to the catch-up rate is right, and PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED is the honest verdict.

⛔ WHAT MUST NOT SHIP AS WRITTEN IS THE VALUE 1, AND THE REASON IS THE ONE THING THE REPORT NEVER LOOKED AT: THE OBSERVATION CADENCE. `HUB_RAMP_TICKS_PER_FRAME` is not a playback rate, it is a ratio between sim ticks and DRAWS — and the draw side is `main.ts:4014`, called once per rendered frame, while `main.ts:2673/2697` drains 0 to 3 sim ticks per rendered frame behind a 0.05 s clamp. At 3, the worst case advances exactly one plate per draw and nothing can ever be skipped, on any machine. At 1, a 30 Hz frame shows every second plate and a hitch-clamped frame shows every third — which breaks the other half of R182-D (*'you don't skip them'*, SPARK_CANON.md:301), a documented owner ruling, on the owner's own screen. And it breaks it INVISIBLY: the report nominates `structureRamp.test.ts:358` as the regression hold that guarantees 'quicker must not become skipped', but that loop increments `tick` by exactly 1 per observation, so it hardcodes the very ratio production does not guarantee. That is the S182 §2 hole exactly — a guard that proves the arithmetic exists while the failing path never consults it.

⭐ THE FIX IS STILL ONE CONSTANT. MAKE IT 2, NOT 1, AND THE REPORT'S OWN EVIDENCE ARGUES FOR IT. At 2 the run is 46 ticks = 0.77 s at 30 fps — still the 1.5× the owner asked for and comfortably inside R182-D's *'within like one second'*; it preserves the 1-tick lead-in the owner explicitly requested, which per=1 deletes (the report's own `per - 1` formula goes to zero at 1 and it never notices); it keeps `structureRamp.test.ts:377-382` GREEN where per=1 turns two assertions red; and it halves the skip exposure, leaving only a 3-tick hitch able to drop a plate. If 0.77 s still reads slow after he looks at it, that is a one-line retune — and the honest thing to write at the constant is that going below 2 trades plates-on-screen for speed on any machine not drawing 60 fps, which is a decision for him and not for a session.

What a branch must be handed on top of the report: the 18th file (`e2e/hub-ramp-art.spec.ts:237`), the two red assertions, the `hubSelfDestructS182.test.ts:345` coverage re-pin, the 23-vs-24 tick off-by-one before it reaches SPARK_CANON.md §7, and the instruction to write the new budget test against a 2-and-3-tick observation cadence rather than 1 — because that is the only test in this whole change that would have caught the thing the report missed.
